newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Fortune and Fame set for a comeback.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Fortune and Fame set for a comeback.

text.p: Curragh-based trainer Dermot Weld on Monday revealed that top-flight hurdler Fortune And Fame is set to return to action in a fortnight.
Weld said he is delighted with his stable-star's progress after a lengthy lay-off and he will aim him the 10-year-old at the Guinness Arkle Challenge Trophy at Cheltenham in March.

Fortune and Fame, twice winner of the AIG Europe Champion Hurdle at Leopardstown and fourth to Alderbrook in the Champion Hurdle two seasons ago, has not run since he scored at Punchestown in April, 1995.

"He has had problems with the tendons in his legs all his life but he is progressing well in his comeback. He schooled very well over fences the other morning and, all being well, he will run in a novice chase in around a fortnight," Weld said.

"If we can get him right he is very talented horse as he won the Irish Champion Hurdle twice. His jumping is superb, it always has been. He has been entered for the Arkle and fingers crossed we can keep him sound," he added.
Injury has bedevilled Fortune And Fame's career and forced him to miss the Cheltenham Festival in both 1993 and 1994.
In the latter year he was ante-post favourite for the Smurfit Champion Hurdle, sponsored by his owner, until cast in his box days before the race and he had to be withdrawn.
